_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
REF — A WHOLE NUMBER IS A HANDBOOK PAGE, ITS DECIMALS ARE THE JOBS ON IT. Mike's
ruling, 2026-09-23: page 7 is the Advisory Engine, so 7.1/7.2/7.3 are engine jobs and
NOTHING else may start with 7. A new job on an existing page takes the next free
decimal of that page. A JOB WITH NO PAGE MEANS THE FEATURE HAS NOT EARNED ONE YET -
the page is written first, and takes the next free page number. The register is
design/features/README.md; the rule is design/PAGE-NUMBERS.md.
TAKE A NEW NUMBER FROM `npm run check:branch`, NEVER from this file. It reads every
machine's branch; this file is one branch's view and cannot see the other's. Guessing
produced ELEVEN duplicated refs - 4.81, 4.88-4.92 and 4.94 each name two unrelated
jobs in the archive, where the uniqueness guard below does not reach.
2.x, 3.x, 4.x and 5.1-5.5 ARE CLOSED FAMILIES - the old flat scheme, frozen as history
because 613 references to those numbers are written into 279 code files. Never reissue
one, and never renumber one.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.risk: A firm whose owners add their own tasks gets a table running under the page's running foot on the client's plan - the fault fixed once already on 2026-09-25 at ten tasks. Nothing is lost; the page just prints badly.

items.name: Conversion is per model, and no model states which currency its figures are in
items.scoreReason: robustness - the figures are right, but nothing on screen says which currency they are in
items.why: Mike ruled 2026-09-22 that currency is a FIRM setting and conversion belongs inside a model where a primary currency is already entered. The forecast already works that way via fxAllowancePct. No model SAYS so on screen.
items.risk: A model carrying a foreign leg shows a converted figure beside an unconverted one with nothing distinguishing them, and an advisor cannot tell which is which. No wrong number today - the maths is right and every foreign leg has an fx input. The risk is the next model with a foreign leg being built with no input and nobody noticing.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-22 - in his own words, after both limits were shown to him as recorded boundaries rather than tasks: "lets be clear - BOTH those issues must be fixed, add them to the to do list."

items.note: ✅ CHECKED 2026-09-22, AND THERE IS NO WRONG NUMBER: every model with a foreign leg already takes an fx input. All 30 files in server/report/ were scanned - only the forecast and the import model have one, both are fx-aware, and multiplePropertyModel matched only on the Google Sheets function Import Range. 🔴 SO THE JOB IS THE RULE AND THE LABEL, NOT THE MATHS: write Mikes rule into the localisation Brief and into ADDING-A-REPORT so the next foreign-leg model is asked, and say on screen which currency a converted figure is in. Wording is his.

items.why: Formal strategic planning starts by assessing the current position - staff, customer and supplier feedback, financial analysis, economic outlook. The three-way forecast and the performance reports already hold much of the financial half, and nothing carries it across.
items.risk: An advisor retypes figures the app already holds, or skips the assessment. The review must also say what CANNOT be imported: staff, customer and supplier feedback and the economic outlook are named by Mike as part of the same component, and no report in this app holds any of them.

items.name: Wordsmith - turning what the client said into statements they can use
items.scoreReason: a facilitator tool, not a gate on the session
items.why: In a planning session the advisor and client talk an idea through and then have to write it down well. Wordsmith renders what they discussed into meaningful statements, or helps craft a powerful message.
items.risk: It writes client-facing wording, so its output is never structured data and must be shown for approval before it lands anywhere. If it ever reads spoken content rather than the typed boxes, that is personal data - only Meeting Review is cleared to send that, and extending it is a fresh decision for Mike, never an inference from that one.

items.name: Devil's Advocate - challenging optimistic thinking in the room
items.scoreReason: a facilitator tool, not a gate on the session
items.why: A planning conversation drifts optimistic and nobody in the room is paid to disagree. Devil's Advocate asks the hard questions and challenges over-optimistic thinking, backed by known business concepts and market analysis data.
items.risk: It argues with the client in front of the advisor, so its tone and its evidence both matter. "Market analysis data" needs a named source: this app holds none, and an AI asserting market facts without one commits the exact error the feature exists to catch.

items.name: Meetings longer than about 27 minutes are too big for OpenAI and lose their audio
items.why: The end-of-meeting pass sends the whole recording to OpenAI as one file, OpenAI refuses files over 25 MB, and the browser records about 0.9 MB a minute, so a normal client meeting will not transcribe.
items.risk: The audio is deleted whether or not transcription worked, so an advisor who records an hour-long meeting ends with no transcript and no recording to retry. Near-certain rather than proven: the 25 MB cap is OpenAI's stated limit and the rate was measured on 2026-09-24, but no 30-minute recording has been sent.

items.name: Review imported-stock FX in the forecast and import model: supplier currency and exchange rate
items.why: Paying an overseas supplier is the one place in the app where both a foreign currency and an exchange rate genuinely apply. Today the forecast uses neither: it adds a flat percentage allowance, 10% by default, to the landed cost.
items.risk: An importer's cash forecast shows stock payments as the home-currency cost plus a guessed percentage, not what the supplier's invoice will actually cost at a stated rate. A rate move or a supplier invoicing in another currency is invisible, and the deposit and balance timing in the forecast carries the same guess.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-24 - in his words: "we have an input for fx (foreign exchange) payments for stock, imported from overseas, in the 3 way forecast and import model... this is ONE area where BOTH the currency and the exchange rate will need to apply - make it a task to review this please"

items.touches: server/report/threeWayForecastModel.js (fxAllowancePct and salesFxAllowancePct, fxOnPurchases, fxOnSales, the deposit and balance lines near 1068-1137); server/report/importShipmentModel.js, which defers exchange to the forecast; their intake screens and golden tests; item 13.2, which labels the currency of a converted figure.
items.note: A REVIEW FIRST, NOT A BUILD. Established 2026-09-24 from the code: no supplier currency and no exchange rate exist in either model - only a percentage allowance on purchases and a matching one on overseas sales. The review should settle what the advisor enters (supplier currency, rate, and whether the allowance stays as a buffer on top), and run the impact test before any design. Firm currency stays a firm setting - Mike's ruling 2026-09-22, recorded on 13.2.
